## The problem this unit solves

A script becomes a maintainable project when another learner can install it, run it, test it, and understand its boundaries.

## Questions to carry through the unit

- What input, state, and output can you identify before running the code?
- Which boundary makes the next change easier to explain and test?
- What evidence would distinguish a correct result from a lucky one?

## Learning sequence

### 1. Define project boundaries

Separate reusable modules from entry points and choose a readable layout.
### 2. Make execution repeatable

Record dependencies, isolate an environment, and accept command-line arguments.
### 3. Protect behavior

Write focused pytest tests and use formatting, linting, and type checking.
### 4. Automate the agreement

Run the same checks with pre-commit locally and CI after sharing changes.

## Unit checkpoint

After every lesson, complete the [required unit checkpoint](checkpoint.qmd).
It asks you to combine the unit skills in one small artifact rather than recall
each lesson separately.
